title: Compatibility shim: embeddings + streaming tool-calls — unified pagination & error mapping
creator: Ethan Ross
description: Problem: A set of large customers use legacy embeddings/rerank endpoints with cursor-based pagination and expect numeric legacy error codes. New streaming + tool/function calling flows produce mixed event sequences and structured output chunks which break iterator stability and client-side retry logic. Goal: deliver a compatibility shim that preserves cursor idempotency, normalizes/hedges error codes for legacy clients, and provides deterministic pagination markers across streaming + tool-calls and structured-output paths.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy clients (compat-mode header) can iterate embeddings/rerank results across streaming responses and function/tool call invocations without cursor duplication or reordering.

HTTP error mapping: legacy numeric error codes are reliably mapped to canonical HTTP codes and include retry-hints header; mapping documented in spec and test harness covers transient (5xx), rate-limit (429), and semantic (4xx) classes.

Pagination cursors emitted for stream fragments use stable opaque ids and include a monotonic sequence token so clients can resume exactly where they left off even when a tool call was injected mid-stream.
No regressions for modern clients: structured-output schemas remain unchanged when compat header absent; throughput/latency within 5% of baseline in synthetic load tests.
Migration guide and client-side adapter snippets (JS/Go/Python) published to docs with example conversion for common SDKs.
End-to-end test suite covering at least: stream -> toolcall -> resume, stream cancellation -> idempotent retry, pagination tombstones and cursor replay semantics.
Rollout plan for enabling compat_mode by default for specific legacy accounts after validation and telemetry thresholds met.
implementation_notes: Introduce HTTP header X-Redwood-Compat-Version with semantic versioning; default absent means modern behavior.

Emit cursor metadata as base64-encoded JSON string: {"v":2,"seq":<int>,"origin":<stream|batch>,"tombstone":<0|1>} — note: shim will keep opaque to clients but server-side validators will parse for resume logic.
When streaming with tool/function calls, mark tool-call boundaries with a stable marker event (compat_marker) that advances seq without exposing structured payload to legacy clients.

Error mapping table: numeric legacy codes -> HTTP mapping file in repo (examples: 1001->429 with Retry-After hint, 2003->503 transient, 3002->422 validation). Include Retry-After and X-Redwood-Retry-Advice headers for guidance.
Client hint header X-Redwood-Expect-Idempotency allows clients to opt into receiving idempotency tokens for long-running iterator sessions.
Fallback behavior: if a legacy client resumes with a cursor referencing a tombstoned token, return 410 with human-readable migration hint and link to migration guide.
Telemetry: emit compat.mode, compat.version, resumed_from_tombstone, error_map_applied, stream_tool_boundary events to observability pipeline for rollout metrics.
Add integration tests that run against the dedicated runtime to validate kernel-level behavior does not reorder tokens under batching pressure.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable compat_mode for internal infra and 5 small legacy accounts; monitor error-map-applied ratio and resume-success metric for 7 days.
Phase 2 (expanded): enable for 20 enterprise customers that reported breaking changes; collect SDK telemetry and manual feedback from SEs.
Phase 3 (opt-in to opt-out): enable in hosted for all accounts with X-Redwood-Compat-Version=1.0; allow opt-out via Console toggle tied to account feature flag.

Phase 4 (default disable): do not enable by default until metrics indicate <0.1% resume failures and no significant perf regressions; then flip default for accounts older than 2024 with migration grace window.
test_plan: Unit: cursor encode/decode roundtrip, error mapping table lookups, compat header parsing.
Integration: simulated streaming endpoint that injects tool-call boundaries mid-iterator and validates resume points across reconnections.
E2E: SDK adapter tests (JS/Python/Go) that demonstrate migration path code samples, run in CI against staging runtime.
Load: run synthetic load with realistic token distributions to verify no >5% latency regression and confirm batching honors seq monotonicity.
Chaos: inject transient 5xxs, connection resets and validate client replay yields no duplicate items and correct dedupe behavior.
activity: 2026-02-25 - Ethan Ross created ticket with initial problem statement after customer SE reported duplicate cursor items when using legacy SDK during a streaming rerank flow.
2026-02-27 - Sync with runtime and SDK leads; agreed to prototype compat_marker events and cursor seq field. Action: ENG to spike (ENG-94120).
2026-03-03 - Design review: UX for Console toggle discussed; decided to surface migration hints in Console and API error payloads. Assigned to Maya for rollout docs.

2026-03-06 - Engineering update: prototype implemented in staging; initial tests show resume success but elevated p95 under certain batching configurations. Follow-up: kernel scheduling tweak planned (ENG-77521).
2026-03-10 - Draft migration guide posted to Drive; added JS/Go adapter snippets. Performance regression reduced after batching tweak; still running expanded canary.
notes: This ticket must coordinate closely with SDK teams — breaking changes to cursor semantics require adapter snippets and automated codemods for customers embedding old SDKs.
Keep compat-mode parsing server-side only; avoid exposing cursor internals in public docs to preserve ability to iterate schema in future.
We should consider a follow-up to unify embed + search pagination across Vector Search Gateway if this shim proves stable.
